band.heading: The band
bio: Dorothy's Dishes is an Americana and folk‑rock band from Lincoln, Nebraska. Formed in 2020, it's old‑school country storytelling straight from the parlor: country folk with bluegrass roots, acoustic features with smooth harmonies, and just enough upbeat rockabilly to keep your toe tappin'.
Tim McCarty formed the band and partnered with Cari McCullough as his co‑lead. Stepping into a long line of troubadour tradition, the two blend harmonies over Tim's lyrical songwriting.

The band's second album, Flatwater Revival, includes "Road Trippin' Nebraska," a song and video that packs nearly 200 Nebraska towns and landmarks into three minutes and went further than any of them expected.

namingStudy.title: Naming Study: Findings and Recommendation
memo: Sometime in 2020, before the second cup of coffee

sections.label: Section 1
sections.heading: Executive summary
paragraphs: The client proposed naming the band after its two lead singers. We tested this name with twelve members of the public. Eleven of them believed they were being asked about an Irish folk cover band. The twelfth asked whether this was a law firm and, when told it was not, said "that's a shame."
We do not recommend proceeding with "McCarty & McCullough." We recommend the alternative described in Section 5, which tested as "alliterative, but in a way that made people hungry."

sections.label: Section 2
sections.heading: Method
paragraphs: Twelve participants were recruited from the parking lot of a grocery store in Lincoln, Nebraska, with the offer of a free doughnut. Each was shown the name on a plain white card and asked to describe, in their own words, what the band probably sounded like. Participants were then shown a photograph of the band (Appendix B) and asked whether it changed their answer. It did not.
One participant left before the study concluded, citing "the fiddle thing." His partial responses are included in Appendix A.

findings.label: Section 3
findings.heading: Key findings
findings.intro: When asked what "McCarty & McCullough" most likely was, participants answered as follows:

chart.label: Irish folk band, but original songs

findings.chartNote: Percentages exceed the number of participants because one respondent answered twice, both times with "is this a law firm."
bullets: Nine participants asked, unprompted, whether there was a fiddle.
Six participants assumed the band played primarily on or around St. Patrick's Day.
Four participants said the name sounded like "the credits of a movie where a horse dies."
Two participants could not stop saying it in an accent. They were asked to stop. They did not stop.

items.text: "Is this the two guys who do the Pogues thing at the Irish pub? Because I like them. I'd go see them."
items.who: Participant 2, on being told it was not the two guys: "Well, now I'm disappointed."

items.text: "Sounds like a firm that handles slip‑and‑fall cases. But only in Dublin."
"There's a fiddle, right? There has to be a fiddle. Just tell me about the fiddle."
"Wait, it's country? Then why don't they just say that? Call it Dorothy's Dishes or something. I'm just saying words now."
items.who: Participant 11, who has never been thanked

alternatives.label: Section 5
alternatives.heading: Alternatives tested
rows: Worse. Two participants asked if it was a podcast. Another said it sounded "vaguely psychedelic."
Strong recall. Legal advised against it in a tone we did not appreciate.
Tested very well. Rejected by the band on the grounds that it is "not a name."
71% "confused but curious." 22% "hungry." 7% asked who Dorothy is and were told it's a long story, which they accepted.
alternatives.recommendation: Recommendation. Proceed with "Dorothy's Dishes." It does not describe the music. It does not describe the band. It has, however, never once made anyone ask about a fiddle, and at this point we consider that the primary success metric.

transcript.label: Appendix A
transcript.heading: Participant 7, partial transcript
lines: What kind of music do you think this band plays?
Let's set the fiddle aside for a moment.
What if I told you there is no fiddle?
Then what are the two of them doing.
One writes the songs and plays guitar. The other sings.

stimulus.label: Appendix B
stimulus.heading: Stimulus image
stimulus.alt: Sepia photograph of four band members in old-fashioned suits and hats, one woman in a prairie dress, two antique guitars
stimulus.caption: Stimulus B, shown to all participants after the name card. Did not help. If anything, participants became more certain about the fiddle.

namingStudy.closing: This report was prepared at considerable expense and was, in the end, agreed with.
